string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of China and the country\'s political, cultural and educational centre. With a history stretching back over three thousand years, it served as the imperial capital for several dynasties. The city is home to world-famous landmarks such as the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, the Summer Palace and sections of the Great Wall. Its traditional hutong alleyways and courtyard houses sit alongside modern skyscrapers and Olympic venues. Beijing hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and the 2022 Winter Olympics, making it the first city to stage both events. Today it has more than twenty-one million residents.

Shanghai is China\'s largest city and one of the world\'s most important financial and trading centres. Located at the mouth of the Yangtze River, its port is among the busiest container ports on the planet. The city is famous for the historic Bund waterfront and the futuristic skyline of Pudong, where the Oriental Pearl Tower and Shanghai Tower dominate the view. Once divided into foreign concessions, Shanghai blends European-style architecture with traditional Chinese lanes and ultramodern districts. It hosted the 2010 World Expo and is home to more than twenty-four million people, making it a symbol of China\'s rapid economic growth.

Chongqing is a sprawling municipality in southwest China and the largest of the four by area and population. Built on steep hills at the meeting point of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers, it is nicknamed the Mountain City, and its dramatic layered skyline has made it a social-media sensation. Chongqing is renowned across China for its fiery hotpot cuisine. Historically it served as China\'s wartime capital, and today it is a major manufacturing and transport hub and the gateway to Yangtze River cruises through the Three Gorges. More than thirty-two million people live within the municipality\'s boundaries.

Tianjin is a major port city in northern China, about thirty minutes from Beijing by high-speed train. Located where the Hai River meets the Bohai Sea, it has long been one of the country\'s most important gateways for trade. In the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, foreign concessions gave the city a distinctive European flavour, still visible today in the Italian Style Town and the Five reat Avenues district. Modern attractions include the Tianjin Eye Ferris wheel, Ancient Culture Street and the fast-growing Binhai New Area. Tianjin is famous for local snacks such as goubuli buns and jianbing, and is home to around fourteen million residents.
